pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:0.5: 1. The training rule on storing bowls
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:0.6: “These thirty rules on relinquishment and confession come up for recitation.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.1: At one time the Buddha was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.2: Now at that time the group of six nuns were accumulating many bowls.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.3: People walking around the dwelling saw him and complained and criticized him,
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.4: “How could the nuns do this? They are hoarding many bowls! They are trading in bowls! They are pawning bowls! “
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.5: The bhikkhunīs heard the men grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.6: Some bhikkhunīs who were modest … criticized and complained and spread it about:
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.7: “How can the nuns from the group of six store bowls?” …
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.8: “Is it true, monks, that the nuns of the group of six are storing up almsbowls?”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.9: “Is it true, monks, as they say,
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.11: “How could the nuns from the group of six store bowls? …
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.12: This is not for the purpose of confidence in those without confidence …
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.13: And thus, too, the nuns should recite this training rule:
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:1.14.1: “If a nun makes a stock of almsbowls, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.4: … and so on … This is the bhikkhunī meant in this context.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.6: Two bowls—a metal bowl, an earthenware bowl.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.7: There are three kinds of bowl: The best bowl, the middling bowl, and the worst bowl.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.9: He takes a full handful, a quarter of a mouthful, and what is appropriate as condiment.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.10: The middle one, called the middle
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.11: He takes rice, four parts of which are boiled rice, and a suitable curry.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.13: He takes the food, eating it in four parts, and the appropriate sauce.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.14: Then, the one of the highest grade is the one who has gone to the world of the Thirty-three. The one who has gone to the world of the Thirty-three is the one who has gone to Tuṣita.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.18: When the dawn appears, it becomes subject to relinquishment.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.19: It should be given to the Sangha, or to a group, or to one bhikkhunī.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.20: And it should be relinquished like this, monastics.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.21: That nun should approach the Sangha, put her upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect at the feet of the senior nuns, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say this:
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.22: “Venerables, this bowl of mine has been kept overnight. It is to be relinquished. I relinquish it to the Sangha.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.23: Having given him up, he should confess the offense.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.24: If a nun who is capable consents, the offense should be acknowledged.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.25: The bowl should be given to him.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.26: “Let the Sangha listen to me, sisters.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.27: This bowl belongs to the nun named so-and-so. It has been relinquished to the Sangha.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.28: If it seems appropriate to the Sangha, the Sangha should give this bowl to the nun so-and-so”.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.29: The nun should approach several nuns, put her upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect at the feet of the senior nuns, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say this:
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.30: “This robe-cloth, Venerables, worn by me past the time limit, I give back to you.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.31: When it has been put aside, the offense should be confessed.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.32: If an offense is to be acknowledged, it should be acknowledged by a regular nun who is capable.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.33: The bowl should be thrown away.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.35: This bowl belongs to the nun named so-and-so. It has been relinquished to the nuns.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.36: If it seems appropriate to the venerable ones, the venerable ones could give this bowl to the nun named so-and-so.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.37: The nun should approach another nun, put her upper robe over one shoulder, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.38: “Venerable, this robe-cloth was worn by me after the robe season and is to be relinquished.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.39: I give this up to you, venerable.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.40: If one has put it down, one should confess the offense.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.41: The nun must admit the offense.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.42: The bowl should be given to him without the contents.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.1.43: “I offer this bowl to the Venerable.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.1: If, when the time has passed, he perceives that it has passed, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.2: If the robe is more than a league away and one is unsure, one commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.3: If she has gone past the limit and she perceives that she has,
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.4: If it is not his own, and he perceives it as not his own, he commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.5: Having caused to be made, perceiving it as not caused to be made, there is an offence entailing relinquishment and confession.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.6: If one does not relinquish, but perceives one has relinquished, there is an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.7: He perceives what is not wrong as wrong.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.8: He perceives what is not destroyed as destroyed …
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.9: Having made a division in the undivided, one perceives a division.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.10: If one who is not separated from the robe thinks she is separated, then for each day she is not separated, she commits an offense entailing relinquishment and confession.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.11: If without having given back the bowl, he uses it, he commits an offense of wrong conduct.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.12: When the threshold has been crossed, but one perceives that it has not, one commits an offense of wrong conduct.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.13: When it is a rattan mat, and there is uncertainty, there is an offense of wrong conduct.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.2.14: If the person is not fully clothed, but one perceives that he or she is, there is no offense.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:2.3.2: If it is red at the end, he determines, exchanges, gives away, it is lost, destroyed, broken, they take it after cutting, they take it with trust,
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:3.1: At that time the six groups of nuns did not give a bowl that had been dropped.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:3.2: They told the Blessed One the meaning of this.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:3.3: “Monks, a discarded bowl should not be given.
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:3.4: Whoever does not give, commits an offense of wrong conduct.”
pli-tv-bi-vb-np1:3.5: The first training rule is finished.
